2  JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Sri.
Mutturaju C. in the road traffic accident that took place on 13.05.2023.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 13.05.2023 at about 09.10 a.m. when the deceased was sitting on his two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-42-E-4245 near Mayaganahalli, on Bangalore - Mysore service road, Ramanagara Dist., at that time the driver of the Toyoto Etios vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-3632 came from Mysore side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased's vehicle.
Due to impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Ramanagara Dist., Government Hospital for first aid, then shifted to NIMHANS hospital,
Bangalore and died on the way to Victoria Hospital, Bangalore.

Thereafter, the dead body was shifted to General Hospital, Ramanagara wherein post-mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and funeral expenses.
3. It is stated that the deceased was aged about 30 years and was working in as a Employee in private company and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.

It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Toyoto Etios vehicle bearing Reg.No.
KA-10-A-3632.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
4. Inspite of service of summons, the respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared before the court through their respective counsel.
Inspite of granting sufficient time, the respondent No.1 did not file his written statement and the respondent No.2 filed it's written statement.
5. The 2nd Respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.

This respondent has not disputed about issuance of Policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending Toyoto Etios vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 10-A-3632, however, restricted its liability subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, provision of MV Act, valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of the offending vehicle, valid RC, Permit and FC and also subject to the confirmation of Sec.64 VB of the insurance Act.
Respondent also seeks protection under section 147 and 149 of M.V. Act.
It has also contended that owner and jurisdictional police have not complied the Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act.
Also there is no involvement of alleged offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the Yashodha.G vs Karthik.N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31039442/
3 offending vehicle.
Further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioners are excessive and exorbitant.
Hence on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

6. Based on the pleadings, this court has framed following issues:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that on 13.05.2023 at 9.10 a.m. when the deceased was sitting on his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-E-4245, near Mayaganahalli,
Bengaluru - Mysuru service road, Ramanagara Dist., at that time, the driver of the Toyoto Etios vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-3632 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased motor cycle, caused the accident, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Mutturaju C.?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 14 documents.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced their evidence.
8. Heard the arguments.

9. My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.3 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4 ...

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1: It is the case of the petitioners that, on 13.05.2023 at about 09-10 a.m. when the deceased was sitting on his two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-42-E-4245 near Mayaganahalli, On Bangalore - Mysore service road, Ramanagara Dist., at that time the driver of the Toyoto Etios vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-3632 came from Mysore side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased's vehicle.
Due to impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Ramanagara Dist., Government Hospital for first aid, then shifted to NIMHANS hospital, Bangalore and then died on the way to Victoria Hospital,
Bangalore.

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the driver of Toyota Etios and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the Yashodha.G vs Karthik.N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31039442/
4 petitioners.
11.

In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, Spot mahazar, Sketch, IMV report, Inquest report, P.M. report and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
12.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of Toyota Etios.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

13. According to the version of petitioners, the accident happened on Bengaluru-Mysuru service road, near Mayaganahalli, Ramanagara Dist, when the driver of Toyoto Etios Car bearing No.
KA-10-A-3632 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased who was sitting on his motorcycle on left side of the road and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P3 being the Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 and Ex.P4 which is the sketch Yashodha.G vs Karthik.N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31039442/
5 prepared at the time of spot mahazer, it reflects that deceased was sitting on his motorcycle on the left side of the road and width of the road 30 feet, the car came from Mysuru towards Bengaluru, the driver of Car in a negligent manner came in high speed and dashed against the deceased's motorcycle which was standing on the left side of the road, due to the said act deceased person fell down on the road and got injured.
If the driver of Car drove it in a normal speed in a service road on observing the vehicles and persons, then he would certainly avoid the accident.
Added more, the contents of Ex.P5 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P8 was also filed as against the driver of the lorry.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the Car driver.

14. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

entities.text: Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending van.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the owner of the Car who is the Respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement and also not cross-examined the PW1 to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the driver of Car and he was charge sheeted.
15. Viewed from any angle this court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent driving of the offending vehicle Car bearing Reg. No. KA-10-A-3632 by its driver.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:

While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the death of Mutturaju C.
was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle said Toyota Etios.

The petitioners claimed that, Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the Mother, Petitioners No.3 is the Father, Petitioner No.4 is the married Sister and Petitioner No.5 is the daughter of the deceased.

Yashodha.G vs Karthik.N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31039442/
6
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of deceased and petitioners No.1 to 5 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been seriously disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners No.1 to 5 are the legal representative and legal heirs of the deceased C. Mutturaju and they are entitled for compensation.
17.
The petitioners have contended that the deceased was working as employee in private company and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In order to prove the same, petitioners have not produced any documents before the court.

Therefore, considering the occupation of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/-
per month.
18. It is stated that the deceased was aged 30 years at the time of the accident.
The petitioners have produced Adhaar card of the deceased at Ex.P9 which shows the date of birth of the deceased as 27-06-1992.
The accident occurred on 13-05-2023.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident is considered as 30 years.

The proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '17'.
19.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 30 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

If 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- i.e. 40%).
20.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the Mother, Petitioners No.3 is the Father,
Petitioner No.4 is the married Sister and Petitioner No.5 is the daughter of the deceased.
So, the petitioner No.4 is not considered as dependent on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, in this case, the deceased died leaving behind 4 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.16,800/- p.m. (Rs.22,400 - Rs.5,600 = Rs.16,800/-).
21.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.16,800/- p.m. and the multiplier '17' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.34,27,200/- (Rs.16,800 X 12 X 17).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.34,27,200/- under the head of loss of dependency.

7 22.

Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.44,000/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
23.
In this case, the Petitioner No.2 is the mother, Petitioner No.3 is father, Petitioner No.4 is the sister and petitioner No.5 is the daughter of the deceased

and as per the decision reported in (2018)
12 SCC 130

in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners No.2 to 5 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of father/son causes great shock and agony to the children and parents of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their father/son.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.44,000 x 4) under the head of Filial consortium.

24. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1. Towards loss of dependency Rs. 34,27,200-00  2. Towards loss of Consortium to the Rs. 44,000-00  petitioner No.1  3. Towards loss to estate Rs. 16,500-00  4. Towards transportation of dead Rs. 16,500-00  body funeral and obsequies ceremony  expenses  5. Towards loss of Filial consortium to Rs. 1,76,000-00  petitioner No.2 to 5(Rs.44,000 x 4)
Total Rs

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.36,80,200/-.
25.

As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1st petitioner is the widow and petitioners No.2 is the Mother, Petitioner No.3 is the father, Petitioner No.4 is the Sister and Petitioner No.5 is the daughter of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 35:15:15:10:25.
26.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it Yashodha.G vs Karthik.N on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31039442/
8 proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
27. Liability:

sentences.text: Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Toyoto Etios vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-3632.
It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs. 36,80,200/- (Rupees Thirty six lakhs eighty thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 35% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 10% Petitioner No.5 - 25% Further it is ordered that, 60% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in her name and remaining 40% of the amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.5 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner with liberty to the petitioner No.1 to draw periodical interest.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P8 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the Car driver.
14. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
Even in the instant case the owner of the Car who is the Respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement and also not cross-examined the PW1 to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the driver of Car and he was charge sheeted.
So, the petitioner No.4 is not considered as dependent on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, in this case, the deceased died leaving behind 4 dependents.
in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners No.2 to 5 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1st petitioner is the widow and petitioners No.2 is the Mother, Petitioner No.3 is the father, Petitioner No.4 is the Sister and Petitioner No.5 is the daughter of the deceased.
Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No.1 to 5 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 35:15:15:10:25.
26.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.

this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.34,27,200/- under the head of loss of dependency.

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.36,80,200/-.

The 2nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 and 2, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs. 36,80,200/- (Rupees Thirty six lakhs eighty thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - 35% Petitioner No.2 - 15% Petitioner No.3 - 15% Petitioner No.4 - 10% Petitioner No.5 - 25% Further it is ordered that, 60% of the amount fallen to the share of the petitioners No.1 is ordered to be deposited in any nationalized bank for a period of 2 years in her name and remaining 40% of the amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioner No.5 is ordered to be deposited in his name vide Fixed Deposit till he attains the age of majority, at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioner with liberty to the petitioner No.1 to draw periodical interest.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
